title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
byline: Beryl Lipton, Aaron Mackey, and Adam Schwartz
summary: EFF opposes a wave of state laws and pending bills (in Arizona, Connecticut, Washington, Illinois, Georgia, Maryland, and Oklahoma) that exempt ALPR data and derived information from public records laws. The post argues such blanket exemptions eliminate vital oversight that has revealed misuse, and proposes a balancing approach using privacy exemptions, redaction, and aggregation/de-identification instead.

key_quotes.quote: We do not support pending bills in Arizona and Connecticut that would block the public oversight capabilities that ALPR information offers.

the wholesale exemption of ALPR information from disclosure under state public records laws would stymie the public's ability to monitor how their government is using powerful and controversial surveillance technology.

These records are not just informational—they are leverage. Communities, journalists, and local officials have used ALPR disclosures to block new deployments, refuse contract renewals, and terminate existing agreements
These laws and bills in seven states are an unwelcome national trend.
